big_story.headline: Defending the Rupee
big_story.subhead: RBI STEPS UP INTERVENTION AS THE CURRENCY FACES INTENSE PRESSURE
paragraphs: The Reserve Bank of India has stepped up its defense of the domestic currency as forex reserves dip significantly over the past month. Policymakers are deploying multiple strategies, including raising the daily CRR requirement to 99% starting from October 16, to manage liquidity and stabilize the exchange rate. These aggressive moves have sparked intense debate among economists regarding how far central bank interventions can go.

As the rupee nears record lows, the central bank is borrowing playbooks from global peers to shore up the currency without sacrificing broader economic growth. Forex reserves have seen a notable drawdown as authorities continuously intervene in currency markets to curb excessive volatility. The ultimate success of these defensive measures will heavily depend on external factors like crude oil prices and foreign portfolio investor flows.

For college finance students and market watchers, understanding these currency dynamics is crucial for grasping modern monetary policy. While supporting the rupee prevents imported inflation, it tests the central bank's policy toolkit and liquidity management. Observers will be closely monitoring upcoming regulatory shifts and reserve adjustments to see how the local currency responds.
big_story.pullbox: The RBI's aggressive defense of the rupee highlights the delicate balance between managing forex reserves and sustaining domestic economic growth.

explains.title: What is Forex Reserve Defense?
paragraphs: Forex reserve defense refers to actions taken by a central bank to protect its national currency from sharp depreciation by buying or selling foreign currencies. When a currency faces heavy selling pressure, the central bank releases US dollars from its accumulated reserves into the market.

In practice, this reduces the circulating supply of local currency or absorbs excess liquidity to make short-term speculation more expensive. While it helps stabilize exchange rates, sustaining these operations over long periods depletes national reserves and requires careful domestic monetary adjustments.

story_1.headline: TCS Q2 profit rises 15 per cent
paragraphs: Tata Consultancy Services has reported a strong performance for the second quarter, with net profit rising by 15 per cent. The company's overall revenue crossed the significant milestone of ₹73,000 crore during the period.
This solid growth underscores robust demand across key verticals and highlights resilient technology spending by enterprise clients in a competitive global market environment.

story_2.headline: DMart Q2 profit rises 9% YoY
paragraphs: Avenue Supermarts, the operator of the popular supermarket chain DMart, announced its financial results for the second quarter. Consolidated net profit rose nearly 9% year-on-year to ₹743 crore.
Driven by steady consumer demand and ongoing store expansion across the country, the company's total revenue recorded a healthy jump of 18% compared to the same period in the previous fiscal year.

story_3.headline: KEC International bags transmission orders
paragraphs: Infrastructure major KEC International has secured new transmission and distribution orders worth ₹1,014 crore in India, further bolstering its expanding order book and regional execution pipeline.

geopolitics.headline: India-EU FTA Hailed as an Absolute Game Changer
paragraphs: The European Union envoy has described the upcoming India-EU Free Trade Agreement as an absolute game changer for bilateral economic and defence ties. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated that Europe now views India as a primary hub for innovation and manufacturing. The initiative highlights a mutual drive to deepen commercial integration amid shifting global trade dynamics.

While official sentiment remains highly positive, negotiators continue working through tariff structures and regulatory standards. For Indian businesses, a successful pact offers strategic access to European markets and increased foreign investment. As both regions prioritize supply chain resilience, the outcome of these negotiations will shape trade policy for years to come.
